description: Edge and state fixtures for the review schemas. `expectedStructural` is what native Test-Json must say about `instance` under `schema`. A `semantic` case is structurally valid on purpose: it records a hole no single-document schema can close, and names the rule that must close it.

cases.why: The smallest legal frozen plan: one run, one slot, no outcomes.
One concern dispatched to a two-model roster: two slots, two ids.
A completed task with zero findings is a clean run, not a missing one.
Every terminal outcome in one envelope, each non-completed task carrying its diagnostic and owning no finding.

tasks.diagnostic: no response within the dispatch window
outside the selected concern set for this scope
never dispatched before the run ended

cases.why: A finding using every optional field, so the closed property set is exercised at its widest.
All four roles, single-segment content-addressed names, digests and byte counts.
A 96-character artifact name, extension included, is the longest the vocabulary permits and must be accepted.
The preflight success object: capability mode carries no run id.
The preflight rejection object CI depends on: exit 2, state incapable.

instance.message: no schema capability on this host

cases.why: Freeze succeeded.
Exit 5 is published-and-degraded, which is why it is a success state with artifacts.

instance.message: published with 2 of 6 tasks not completed

cases.why: Exit 2 is parse/schema/semantic/state rejection.

instance.message: result input does not match the frozen plan

cases.why: Exit 3 is admission and is terminal for that run id.
A run id the engine rejected is never echoed — it is unbounded caller text and not a UUID — so the status records the rejection instead. Always the invalid exit 2.

instance.message: Run id must be a lowercase UUID.

cases.why: Exit 4 is lock/publication/unexpected failure.
RISK-9: a future version must fail closed rather than be read with v1 semantics.
A closed plan has no room for a caller-supplied aggregate.
A frozen plan with no task would make every attendance claim vacuous.
One above the 128 budget maximum.
Run ids are lowercase UUIDs; two casings of one id are two directories.
RISK-2: the frozen plan is written before dispatch, so it cannot carry an outcome.
Task ids are lowercase slugs so a slot cannot be spelled two ways.
A completed task has nothing to explain; a diagnostic there is an attendance claim in prose.
Every non-completed outcome must say why, or a silent failure reads as an empty reviewer.
REQ-3: counts and state are derived from tasks, so there is no aggregate to supply.
The outcome vocabulary is closed.
One character above the 160-character title maximum.
One reference above the eight-reference maximum.
An empty body is an absent body; the property is optional rather than nullable.
REQ-4: concern and model are derived from the finding's task, never restated by the finding.
A manifest name is one confined segment; traversal would point a reader out of the run root.
An absolute path is not a name.
Nested segments are rejected even without traversal.
A publication missing a view is not a publication.
Roles are closed; an unreferenced extra file must not become readable through the manifest.
A digest is 64 lowercase hex characters.
97 characters is one above maxArtifactNameLength; the name pattern alone would still admit it, so maxLength is what rejects it.
The preflight validates no run, so a run id there is a claim about work that never happened.
Exit 5 is degraded by definition; a clean state on it would tell the caller the opposite of the truth.
Exit 5 reports a valid degraded publication; Freeze has not published a run and cannot claim that terminal state.
The exit vocabulary is closed: 0, 2, 3, 4, 5.
Modes are closed to the two the CLI exposes plus the preflight.
A run-mode status that names no run cannot be attributed to one.
A status cannot both name a run and claim its id was rejected; one of the two is a lie.
A rejected run id can only accompany the invalid exit 2: nothing else can have happened to a run that was never identified.
Two different slots share one id. uniqueItems compares whole objects, so the schema accepts it.
cases.semanticRule: Freeze rejects a plan whose task ids are not unique.

cases.why: One concern/model slot planned twice under two ids: the objects differ, so no structural keyword sees it.
cases.semanticRule: Freeze rejects a plan with two tasks for the same concern and declared model.

cases.why: A finding naming a task the run does not contain. Cross-record references are outside a single-document schema.
cases.semanticRule: Publish rejects a finding whose taskId is not in the frozen task set.

cases.why: Only a completed task may own findings; the schema cannot correlate the two arrays.
cases.semanticRule: Publish rejects findings owned by any task whose outcome is not completed.

cases.why: A task naming a model the declared roster does not contain.
cases.semanticRule: Publish rejects a task whose model is not in the run roster.

cases.why: RISK-2: a structurally perfect envelope inventing a task after dispatch. Only the frozen plan digest can catch it.
cases.semanticRule: Publish rejects a task set that is not exactly the frozen plan's, and a planDigest that does not match the frozen plan bytes.

cases.why: RISK-3: maxLength counts UTF-16 code units, so 4096 accented characters are 8192 UTF-8 bytes and still structurally legal.
cases.semanticRule: Publish rejects a body whose UTF-8 byte count exceeds 4096.

cases.why: Every string is inside its maximum length while the object is about 18 KiB of UTF-8.
cases.semanticRule: The emitter drops diagnostics until the status object is at most 8192 UTF-8 bytes.

cases.why: A manifest whose recorded bytes and digest cannot both describe the file it names.
cases.semanticRule: The reader recomputes every digest and byte count and refuses a manifest that does not match the files it points at.
